stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu hits Andhra Pradesh: Two dead, heavy crop and power damage
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu hits Andhra Pradesh: Two dead, heavy crop and power damage
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu has killed at least two people and damaged standing crops across 52,000 hectares after making landfall in coastal Andhra Pradesh.

Amaravati (Andhra Pradesh): At least two people lost their lives on Tuesday when severe cyclonic storm Murasu struck Andhra Pradesh, submerging standing crops across more than 52,000 hectares and damaging over 300 homes alongside key power transmission infrastructure, officials reported.
The cyclone - the second to strike the state within a single week – made landfall during the early hours of Tuesday.
Downpours inundated standing crops across 15 districts, with Krishna, Bapatla and Nandyala suffering the heaviest impact.
Severe to extremely heavy rainfall lashed several locations prior to landfall.
Strong winds uprooted thousands of trees and damaged 2,750 electricity poles.
High winds and heavy rain severely disrupted power transmission lines, electrical sub-stations, and primary distribution systems, particularly across Prakasam and Bapatla districts.

Prakhar Jain, Managing Director of the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), informed PTI that two cyclone-related fatalities had been recorded in the state, with 12,230 people currently accommodated in emergency cyclone shelters.
Preliminary assessments indicate the cyclone has caused financial losses of at least ₹344 crore in the state, affecting 52,459 hectares of agricultural land, according to Jain.
A total of 312 residential structures sustained damage.
Authorities are monitoring 814 minor irrigation tanks, with 776 placed on high alert status.
Several fishing vessels were wrecked off the Prakasam coast.

stories.headline: Assam: Dikhow River Erosion Threatens 8 Villages with Flood Disaster
stories.title: Assam: Dikhow River Erosion Threatens 8 Villages with Flood Disaster
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NAZIRA: Severe erosion has affected a portion of the embankment along the Dikhow river near Houkajan Satra at Mathiachiga in Nazira, triggering serious concern among residents over the threat of a major flood disaster.
Following the devastating flood of the Dikhow river on July 19, a substantial portion of the embankment in front of the residence of a resident, Bijit Mahanta, was washed away by the strong current.

Residents fear that if the damaged section is not repaired before the next monsoon season, several villages, including Houkajan Satra, Bhakat Gaon, Mathiachiga, Dihingia Gaon, Mechagarh, Naosalia, Jaysagar, and Rajmao, could face severe flooding.
The damaged embankment has also disrupted road connectivity, causing immense hardship to residents, students, and patients who depend on the route for transportation.
Although villagers have levelled the eroded portion with soil to facilitate the movement of students, the road remains unsuitable even for small vehicles.

According to residents, they had already informed Nazira MLA Mayur Borgohain and the Executive Engineer of the Water Resources Department about the alarming situation and requested immediate intervention.
However, they alleged that neither the MLA nor senior departmental officials had visited the affected site so far to assess the extent of the damage.

stories.headline: Nasdaq futures slump over 400 points after midterm election trends point to Democrat sweep
stories.title: Nasdaq futures slump over 400 points after midterm election trends point to Democrat sweep
stories.summary: CNBC's election desk projects that the control of the US House "leans Democratic" and that Democrats will win a minimum of over 200 seats from the Chambers 435, while Republicans could win at least 160.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: CNBC's election desk projects that the control of the US House "leans Democratic" and that Democrats will win a minimum of over 200 seats from the Chambers 435, while Republicans could win at least 160.

Futures on Wall Street have sharply reversed course on Wednesday, November 4, as early trends from the midterm election results are pointing towards the Democrats gaining control of the House of Representatives, and leading in the Senate race as well.
Nasdaq futures, which at one point, were up 200 points, buoyed by results from chipmaker AMD, reversed course to fall as much as 400 points.
Even the Dow Futures, which at one point, were trading near the flat line, are now trading with losses of close to 250 points.

Benchmark indices on Wall Street ended mixed on Tuesday, November 3, while the Nasdaq futures have edged higher in post-market trading ahead of the midterm election results outcome, which will be declared in a few hours from now.
The Dow Jones ended Tuesday's session with losses of close to 200 points, reversing most of Monday's gains.
The S&P 500 gained 0.4%, Nasdaq Composite gained 0.8%, while the Nasdaq 100 index ended 0.7% higher, but remained in "correction territory."
Why Are The Nasdaq Futures Surging?
Nasdaq 100's futures though, are trading with gains of close to 200 points after strong results, and an equally strong, if not better commentary from AMD and its MD & CEO Lisa Su.
The stock is up 8% in extended trading after its third quarter results beat street expectations, as did the company's guidance for the fourth quarter.
The surge in AMD's shares in afterhours trade comes after the stock had snapped a three-day losing streak during Tuesday's regular session, ending nearly 4% higher.
Macro data that has been reported over the last two days has been very strong, indicating that the US economy and the labor market continue to remain on a firm footing.

stories.headline: Indian-origin Suhas Subramanyam wins re-election to US House from Virginia
stories.title: Indian-origin Suhas Subramanyam wins re-election to US House from Virginia
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: has won re-election to the US House of Representatives from Virginia's 10th Congressional District in the 2026 midterm elections, defeating Republican challenger Dave T Beckwith.
Subramanyam secured 63.16% of the vote, polling 1,73,106 votes, while Beckwith received 34.66%, or 94,990 votes.
Independent candidate Ahsen Mujeeb Malik finished third with 1.99% (5,444 votes), while write-in candidates accounted for the remaining 0.19%.

The victory comes after Subramanyam urged Indian-Americans to participate actively in the midterm elections, saying their votes and voices mattered more than ever amid rising hate and discrimination in the US.
Speaking to ANI after voting at a polling station in Manassas, Virginia, on Tuesday, he said the state was witnessing record turnout and expressed confidence about the Democrats' prospects.
"Well, come out and vote.
Make your voice heard.
Your vote matters more than ever, especially at a time when we're seeing record hate in our community, in our country," he said.
Encouraging Indian-Americans to consider entering politics, Subramanyam drew from his own experience of contesting and winning elections.
"I ran for office and I won.
You can too.
If you want to get involved in the political process, now is the time.

stories.headline: Rajiv-Farooq rigged 1987 polls: Ram Madhav
stories.title: Rajiv-Farooq rigged 1987 polls: Ram Madhav
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 3: BJP national vice president Ram Madhav on Tuesday, in a direct dig at LOP in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and his ally NC leadership, alleged that contrary to Congress’ accusations (against BJP), it was “former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi joined by the then Chief Minister Dr Farooq Abdullah, who had massively rigged assembly elections in 1987, leading to emergence of terrorism in J&K.” Referring to the Congress’ allegations against the Modi government of “committing electoral frauds”, Madhav asserted, “In fact, in the history of the country, only two Prime Ministers actually committed such proven electoral frauds. One was Rahulji’s grand-mother Indira Gandhi, whose election was declared “void” by Allahabad court proving the charge that the official election machinery was misused by her to emerge victorious. In response, Indira imposed an emergency in the country.” “Secondly in 1987 in J&K assembly elections, Rahul’s father and the then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in league with Farooq Abdullah, who was then J&K Chief Minister had resorted to large-scale irregularities in the election process, leading to emergence of terrorism here (in J&K). These are well-recorded facts,” he maintained. Madhav, accompanied by J&K BJP general secretaries Gopal Mahajan, Baldev Singh Billawaria, chief spokesperson Sunil Sethi and other senior leaders, was addressing a press conference at BJP headquarter, Trikuta Nagar, Jammu. He accused the Congress of attempting to fulfill its avowed objective of “regime change” through “anarchy, violence and riots as it could not win power through democratic means of electoral battle.” “But people are with Modiji and this became evident again during their opposition’s much hyped Ramlila Maidan rally, where 23 parties together could hardly bring 50,000 or 60,000 people against their haughty claims of 1 million people. BJP, even in a normal rally in an assembly constituency of Jammu, can bring 5000 people,” he maintained. With regard to questions about NC rebellion post cabinet expansion and speculations linking his visit to efforts of BJP government formation, he refused to make any comment. “I’m here to address only the issue related to fake propaganda being run by the opposition on Special Intensive Revision (SIR) across the country and particularly in the union capital. For the past few months, the main opposition party Congress and its leader Rahul Gandhi have been busy spreading lies that the Election Commission has manipulated the country's electoral system,” Madhav said. “The Election Commission will reply to these allegations and they have already submitted a detailed affidavit in the Supreme Court vis-a-vis entire process of SIR and all facts related to it. But we want to expose Congress’ real intentions behind the controversy they wilfully created to achieve its objective of “regime-change” but not through democratic means. Their leaders are spelling out openly at every public forum and social media that they wanted regime-change like it happened in Bangladesh and Nepal,” he said. It was because the opposition had realised that they could not defeat BJP, the Prime Minister Narenda Modi electorally, so they (Congress and other opposition parties) wanted to overthrow democratically-elected regime and wrest power through anarchy, creating doubts about constitutional institutions, Madhav alleged. “However, the people of India will never allow the Congress to succeed in its intentions to spread anarchy in the country,” he asserted. Madhav described all allegations of Congress regarding SIR exercise, presently underway in many parts of the country and already completed in several states, as “out and out white lies.” BJP national vice president reiterated that the Election Commission, through constitutional exercise SIR, was actually cleansing the electoral system of “all sins of Congress which fiddled with the electoral rolls during the past several decades.” He asserted that the Congress's politics of confusion, confrontation and institutional distrust would not succeed in India. Madhav stated the SIR exercise, being undertaken after nearly two decades, was a legitimate democratic process in which Booth Level Officers (BLOs) were conducting door-to-door verification to ensure the accuracy and integrity of electoral rolls and identify illegal entries, including those of foreign nationals residing illegally in India. He alleged that the Congress wanted illegal voters to remain on electoral rolls because its political calculations depended on manipulating the electoral environment. He said the opposition's repeated allegations against constitutional institutions were part of a larger conspiracy to create street unrest and engineer political instability, drawing parallels with developments in neighbouring Bangladesh and Nepal. Regarding Congress’ main allegation that the names of 13 crore voters were deleted (through SIR exercise), Madhav questioned why it could not bring those people to the fore. “Where are those 13 Cr voters whose names, according to the Congress, have been deleted? SIR is cleansing electoral rolls of discrepancies through constitutionally valid SIR exercise, happening after a gap of 20 years. The names of dead (around 2-3 Cr), transferred (around 6 Cr), non-existent voters (1 or 2 Cr) and infiltrators who are illegal voters have been deleted and are being deleted. Like in Jammu, Rohingyas have settled at many places. The names of such infiltrators, illegal immigrants get deleted. This is imperative. Does the Congress want those infiltrators to be included in the electoral rolls as its prospective voters,” he threw a poser. He asserted that one to two crore people, who were genuine voters yet their names were deleted through computer based mechanism, could go and get their names included in the electoral rolls as per the set procedure and there was no bar on it. He alleged that earlier Congress was blaming EVMs for its defeats but could not establish the charge and currently, it was accusing BJP of stealing mandate through “vote-Chori.” “Between 2014 and 2024, the Congress lost 56 assembly polls and three parliamentary elections i.e., 2014, 2019 and 2024. But that time present Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was not there. Then how was Congress defeated? They (Congress) have no logic and it is resorting to political conspiracy. The government is willing to convene a special Parliament session but they (opposition) are running away. They are only trying to provoke people through false propaganda,” Madhav alleged. He mocked that the Congress was crediting BJP for its electoral victories in Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana stating that they were made to win by it (BJP) so that it (BJP) could “justify its electoral fraud in other states and parliamentary polls.” “Nothing could be more ridiculous than this illogical explanation about their wins through the same electoral system, which they are criticising. This depicts how pitiable their condition is,” he said. Madhav explained that they (Congress) were seeking replacement of EVMs with the ballot papers. In the recent municipal polls conducted through ballot papers in October, Congress could win only two wards out of 42 wards. In MLC elections, which are always conducted through ballot papers, out of 28 seats, BJP-allies won 16 seats and BJP won 13 seats but Congress could win only one seat. Responding to another question, he said that there could be possibilities of some discrepancies or errors in SIR exercise, conducted through computer-based mechanisms. “Those errors can always be rectified. If the names of genuine voters get deleted, they can get their names added in the voter lists through relevant forms. Revision is a constitutional process. In Uttarakhand, where I’m (BJP) Prabhari, names deleted mainly comprised Hindu voters and this happened at some other places. Eligible persons can always get their names included,” he explained.

stories.headline: US mid-terms may help D-Street break free from geopolitical overhang
stories.title: US mid-terms may help D-Street break free from geopolitical overhang
stories.summary: Mumbai: All eyes are on the US mid-term elections, with investors looking for signs on whether the outcome could ease global geopolitical uncertainties, a key factor for the outlook on equities.The elections will determine which party controls the House of Representatives and the Senate for the remaining two years of US President Donald Trump's term."The midterm outcome could influence Indian markets through trade policy, global investor sentiment and currency movements," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services. "If Trump loses control of Congress, greater scrutiny of his tariff policies could ease some trade concerns. If Republicans retain control, existing trade and immigration policies may continue, keeping uncertainty elevated." Initial results are expected in India early on Wednesday morning as polling stations close across US time zones.135516833135516837Historical data show that the Nifty has gained the most over one-, three- and six months after the US midterm elections.Of the seven mid-term polls since 1998, the Nifty has gained five times each in a month, three and six months.Read more: Sebi levies Rs 40 lakh penalty on four entities in Axis MF front-running caseMadhavi Arora, chief economist at Emkay Global Financial Services, said a Democratic-controlled Congress could constrain Trump through legislative checks, but he would retain substantial authority over tariffs, immigration and foreign policy."Fiscal policy is likely to remain expansionary under either outcome, putting a floor under US bond yields," she said. She cautioned that the Iran conflict could re-escalate after the midterms, irrespective of the outcome.Read more: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on WednesdayThe post-election policy direction will matter more than the election result itself, said Ankur Punj, managing director at Equirus Wealth. "Investors should avoid tactical allocation decisions based purely on the US political outcome and remain focused on domestic earnings growth, valuations and asset allocation. The real market drivers for India will be crude, US yields and FII flows," he said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asserts Right to Protest Must Not Lead to Indefinite Occupation of Public Spaces
stories.title: Supreme Court Asserts Right to Protest Must Not Lead to Indefinite Occupation of Public Spaces
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi, Nov 3: The Supreme Court on Tuesday orally observed that the right to protest cannot be exercised by occupying a designated protest site indefinitely, stressing that such places must be allotted for specified periods to ensure that other groups also get an opportunity to exercise their constitutional rights.

A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions arising from the October protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
"You cannot occupy a site for all time to come.
There are other protesters.
Where will the farmers go?
Where will the workers go?
Where will the trade unions go?
Where will the homeless go?
Everybody has a right to protest," the apex court remarked.

It further observed that protest sites must be made available to different groups for designated periods, adding that no organisation could claim an exclusive right over a public space merely because it had occupied it first.
"There may be one site or two, but everybody has a right to protest.
You cannot exclude other people merely because you have occupied the site," the CJI-led Bench said.
